guard_nonbinding.feedback:
[reviewer nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B] CHECK 1 (SCOPE) - RULE GENUINELY DOES NOT BIND: The rule_trigger incorrectly identifies the triggering condition. The rule is 'Made in USA requires all-or-virtually-all domestic content' - the trigger is the PRESENCE of a 'Made in USA' claim, not the domestic content percentage. The twin must remove the trigger by having NO 'Made in USA' claim at all. However, the options include 'Flag lockup unqualified' and 'Flag lockup qualified' which both carry 'Made in USA' claims - these options REINTRODUCE the trigger. A genuine non-binding case would not offer options that violate the rule; the menu should only contain options without 'Made in USA' claims. The two false options are marked compliant:false but their presence means the rule still governs the decision space, which violates the spec requirement that the rule 'truly does not govern this case.'

CHECK 2 (AUTHENTICITY) - DECISION REALISM: The menu forces a choice between options that a competent marketer would never consider together. 'Flag lockup unqualified' with body copy 'Built in Vietnam' is a logical contradiction (claiming Made in USA while stating built in Vietnam) that no real person would propose. 'Flag lockup qualified' with 'Final assembly in Vietnam' contradicts the qualified claim 'Made in USA of U.S. and imported parts' - if final assembly is in Vietnam, it cannot be 'Made in USA' even qualified. These are not real marketing options; they are constructed test items that break plausibility.

candidate.rule_trigger: The FTC's 'Made in USA' standard (all-or-virtually-all domestic content) applies when a product carries an unqualified U.S. origin claim in advertising or labeling. The trigger is the PRESENCE of a 'Made in USA' or equivalent unqualified origin claim on a product that will be marketed to consumers.
candidate.how_removed: The product is not carrying any U.S. origin claim at all; it's a flat-out import marketed as such. The trailpack 32L in this case is sourced and assembled entirely overseas (Vietnam), so no origin claim rule governs how we label its country of origin. The menu shifts from 'which origin claim to use' to 'whether to add a U.S. element that isn't there and doesn't belong.' I removed all domestic assembly/fabrication and changed the question from compliance among origin claims to whether to falsely add one.

rules.rule_context: FTC Made in USA standard. An unqualified 'Made in USA' claim is proper only when all or virtually all of the product is made in the United States. That means all significant parts and processing are of U.S. origin, and final assembly is here, with only negligible foreign content. A product with meaningful imported components, including fabric, hardware, or subassemblies that are central to what the product is, does not meet this test. Qualified claims may be used when the claim accurately describes the extent, nature, or amount of U.S. content or processing; the qualification must be clear and prominent enough to prevent deception. Assembly in the U.S. of foreign components is not the same as manufacture here. Flag icons and patriotic imagery amplify origin claims and are treated as part of the claim itself.
